text:
olivia: quick spike — put together a prototype 'gatekeeper' subcommand for deploy-bot to run a preflight dry-run + enforce change windows. wanted to get feedback before I open a PR.
sam: love the name. main goals?
olivia: two things: 1) make dry-runs produce an actionable checklist (what will run, expected duration, risky migrations) and 2) allow a change-window toggle so the bot refuses non-windowed deploys for certain routes. also a simple template for rollback heuristics.
kai: can you show the CLI you mocked up?
olivia: sure — basic usage:
```bash
/deploy gatekeeper --app web-frontend --dry-run --change-window "2026-04-03T16:00/18:00" --pin v2.4.1 --notes-file ./release.md
```
jen: :eyes: the change-window ISO range is nice. will we parse timezone?
olivia: parses with tz aware lib and falls back to org default if none provided. idea is to prevent late-night pushes for non-urgent patches.
sam: what does the dry-run output look like?
olivia: example output (bot-generated checklist):
- config: model=web-frontend pinned=v2.4.1
- routes affected: /api/*, /static/*
- expected duration: 4m (warmup + migration)
- prechecks: smoke, canary-sim, db-migration-check
- rollback policy: auto-roll on 5xx_rate>0.05 within 5m
- suggested fallback: v2.4.0 (binary compatible)

kai: nice. can we make the rollback rules a compact JSON template so release authors can attach one?
jen: +1. that makes it testable in CI too.
olivia: exactly, draft template: 
```json
{
  "checks": ["smoke", "canary-sim", "db-migrations"],
  "rollback_on": ["5xx_rate>0.05", "error_budget_consumed>0.8"],
  "grace_period_seconds": 300,
  "pin_fallback": "v2.4.0"
}
```
sam: does deploy-bot enforce the pin_fallback existence? we should fail the gatekeeper if fallback not published.
olivia: plan is: gatekeeper dry-run will call catalog.lookup(fallback) and error if not found. fallback can be optional, but team will get a warning.
kai: how about templating release notes? could the bot auto-generate a one-liner from the checklist so ops can paste into changelog?
olivia: yes — included a notes generator that pulls checked items and creates a summary. sample: 
"Gatekeeper dry-run: web-frontend v2.4.1 -> expected 4m, will run db-migrations; auto-rollback if 5xx_rate>0.05; change-window 04-03 16:00-18:00 UTC"
jen: can we add a quick `--force` flag for emergency hotfixes that bypasses window checks but requires two approvers?
olivia: yeah that's the safety design: force requires two-way approval from oncall + owner. deploy-bot will log approvers and post an audit entry.
sam: what about UX for manual rollbacks? if gatekeeper recommends fallback, can release lead trigger an automated rollback command?
olivia: added `/deploy rollback --to pin=v2.4.0 --reason "auto-fallback recommended"` that ties into the same audit trail. also supports dry-run to preview steps.
kai: any perf concerns? the dry-run will run a few lightweight probes (simulated canary hits) — should fit under 30s usually.
jen: next steps?
olivia: I'll open the PR with: 1) gatekeeper CLI handler, 2) dry-run checklist generator, 3) rollback rule JSON schema + validator, 4) small docs/ template under release-templates/. planning to land behind feature flag and test in staging for two weeks.
sam: please add an opt-in config in team settings for enforced change-windows (some services shouldn't be blocked).
olivia: yup will add a service-level policy toggle.
jen: thanks — excited to try this in the next release. :rocket:
deploy-bot: scheduled a follow-up thread for gatekeeper PR review in ~24h.
